official_finding.summary: SkyTruth Cerulean's detector logged a 19.63 km, 3.85 km² slick on this scene (model confidence 0.929). A Cerulean human reviewer classed it 'Vessel, coincident', their strongest class, and Cerulean attributed it to MMSI 212656000, one of three vessels its scorer considered (best collated source score 0.4887).

responsible_parties.name: PANAGIA THALASSINI
responsible_parties.role: vessel SkyTruth Cerulean attributed the slick to; recorded type 'Other', flag Cyprus (MID 212 is consistent)

official_finding.caveat: Another algorithm's output with analyst review, not an investigation: Cerulean attributed the slick to this vessel, and nothing here establishes responsibility. Two co-candidate vessels were also scored (248264000, 210007000). The scene carries other Cerulean slicks that are not this case — 3687317 at 126 km and 3687321 at 76 km, attributed elsewhere, plus two on the adjacent frame; ours is the 19.6 km one. No volume was reported. Cerulean's panel truncates the vessel name; the name given here is the one NOAA AIS broadcasts for MMSI 212656000 in our own scene-time extract, not a lookup of Cerulean's record, so the blind conditions of D31 are intact.

naap_result.origin_summary: Trace seeded from det-01 (4.20 km², the only oil feature). Origin cloud centred at 38.09065 N, 124.01913 W after a ~35.5 km median rewind, with the peak at 38.10541 N, 124.06804 W (4.6 km from the centroid). r50 4.44 km, r90 8.82 km (ensemble precision). Release window is a 16 h search bracket (bounded), 2023-03-16 14:24Z to 2023-03-17 06:24Z, not a measured time. Wind share 0.37. Stage 3: 6 in region → 4 in window → 3 plausible → 3 scored, no abstention. Scores 0.620, 0.345 and 0.046, at 2.34 km, 7.87 km and 14.99 km from the origin peak, from 4, 3 and 4 of 7 components (live weight 0.65/0.50/0.65). `type_prior` is null on all three: every scored candidate scored 1.0 there, so it separated nobody (D28).

assessment.explanation: A miss, and a near miss with a precise cause. The vessel Cerulean names came within 14.3 km of our origin grid peak during the scene pass, at a grid probability of 0.0000 against an r90 of 8.82 km. It did enter the origin bounds — about eight hours after our release window had closed. The window ends 2023-03-17T06:24Z; its pass runs 12:55Z to 15:02Z. The origin extract is the box crossed with the window, so the vessel was absent from it and could not be scored. Our funnel 6 → 4 → 3 → 3 named HORIZON (0.62), with OVERSEAS BOSTON (0.35) and AURORA SB (0.05) behind it. AURORA SB is one of the three vessels Cerulean's scorer considered, but at 0.046 on 4 of 7 components and 14.99 km from the peak, that overlap is not an agreement worth claiming. This is the headline blind case (D31), and it comes out a miss.
assessment.what_would_have_helped: The same thing Jacksonville needed, failing in time rather than in space: the box was right and the window was roughly eight hours too early, so a release window derived from slick age instead of only from ensemble convergence would have put the vessel inside it. A cheaper partial fix: where the window is bounded rather than measured — as it is here, a 16 h bracket — score the hours either side of the bracket too and label them as such, instead of treating the bracket edge as a hard cut.

udgam_result.origin_summary: Origin cloud centred at 38.0906° N, 124.0191° W; half the ensemble lands within 4.44 km and nine in ten within 8.82 km. Release window 2023-03-16T14:24:42Z to 2023-03-17T06:24:42Z (bounded). Stage 3 funnel 6 → 4 → 3 → 3.
